mainTopic: Whether an אתרוג follows לקיטה or חנטה for שביעית; why a לולב has קדושת שביעית though it is wood; and the מחלוקת over 'לכם לאכלה' (soaking, laundering, poultice).
overview: This עמוד finishes a source that treats an אתרוג like a tree for שביעית, which seems to clash with our משנה. The גמרא answers that our משנה follows the vote of the Sages at אושא: an אתרוג follows its picking (לקיטה) for both מעשר and שביעית. It then explains that a line is missing from that ברייתא. The five elders had said שביעית follows the budding (חנטה), and אושא disagreed. Next, the גמרא infers from our משנה that a seventh-year לולב is holy, and asks how that can be if a לולב is just wood. It answers from the פסוק 'לכם לאכלה'. Only things whose benefit and using-up happen together have קדושת שביעית, so fuel wood is excluded but a לולב is not. The גמרא then shows that this rule is a מחלוקת between the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי about using שביעית produce for soaking flax and laundering. It explains how each side reads 'לכם' and 'לאכלה'. The עמוד ends inside a ברייתא asking why laundering is included and a poultice (מלוגמא) excluded, and the answer continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: End of the source that contradicts our משנה about the אתרוג
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the quote of a source the גמרא brought against our משנה. According to רבן גמליאל, an אתרוג is like a vegetable only for tithing, which follows its picking. In everything else, including שביעית, it is like a tree. רבי אליעזר says it is like a tree in every way.
steps.simpleTranslation: …that the time of its picking sets its tithing. These are the words of רבן גמליאל. רבי אליעזר says: an אתרוג is like a tree in every matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of a source it brought to contradict our משנה. That source treats the אתרוג like a tree for שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under both opinions in this source, an אתרוג follows the rules of a tree for שביעית. That means its year is set by when it budded (חנטה), not by when it was picked. Our משנה, however, seems to treat an אתרוג picked in the seventh year as שביעית produce, so the two sources seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Picking or harvesting of the fruit
Tithing, separating מעשר
A tree (here meaning the rules for tree-fruit)
Is equal to, follows the same rules as

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is the second half of a quotation that began on the previous עמוד. The גמרא quoted it to challenge our משנה about buying an אתרוג in שביעית.

phrases.english: that at the time of its picking is its tithing,
phrases.notes: For tithes, an אתרוג is like a vegetable: what counts is when it was picked.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabban Gamliel.
Rabbi Eliezer says:
An etrog is like a tree in every matter.
phrases.notes: Even for tithes, it follows the tree rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁבִּשְׁעַת לְקִיטָתוֹ עִישּׂוּרוֹ, דִּבְרֵי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the contradicting source that was quoted on the previous עמוד.
steps.kashyaTarget: Our משנה, which implies that an אתרוג picked in שביעית counts as שביעית produce
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to this source, an אתרוג is like a tree for שביעית, so its year follows חנטה. A sixth-year אתרוג picked in the seventh year should then be ordinary sixth-year produce.

steps.title: Our משנה follows the Sages of אושא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that our משנה follows a different תנא. According to the vote of the Sages at אושא, an אתרוג follows its picking for both מעשר and שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה follows this תנא, as a ברייתא teaches. רבי יוסי said: אבטולמוס testified in the name of five elders that an אתרוג follows its picking for מעשר. And our Rabbis voted in אושא and said: both for מעשר and for שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. Our משנה agrees with a different opinion: the ruling made at אושא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier source treated the אתרוג like a tree for שביעית. The Sages at אושא ruled that it follows its picking for שביעית too. Our משנה follows אושא, so an אתרוג picked in the seventh year has שביעית status.

keyTerms.meaning: Testified, reported an earlier tradition
They were counted, meaning they took a vote
Usha, a town in the Galil where the Sanhedrin met
Tithe

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the question of whether an אתרוג follows לקיטה or חנטה for שביעית was debated among the תנאים. Our משנה takes the אושא position.

phrases.english: He (our Mishnah) said it like this tanna,
as it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yosei said:
Avtolemos testified in the name of five elders:
An etrog follows its picking for tithes,
and our Rabbis voted in Usha and said:
both for tithes and for the Sabbatical Year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning our משנה to a different תנאי opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה should agree with the source that treats an אתרוג like a tree for שביעית.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה follows the אושא ruling: an אתרוג follows its picking even for שביעית.

steps.title: Who mentioned שביעית?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the wording of the ברייתא. The first half spoke only about מעשר, so why does the אושא ruling add שביעית?
steps.simpleTranslation: שביעית — who mentioned it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a gap in the ברייתא's wording. The phrase "both for מעשר and for שביעית" responds to something that was never said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling at אושא is worded as if it adds to or disagrees with an earlier view about שביעית. But the testimony of אבטולמוס said nothing about שביעית, so the addition seems to come out of nowhere.

keyTerms.meaning: Who mentioned its name? (asked when a topic appears without being introduced)

phrases.english: The Sabbatical Year — who mentioned it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the ברייתא quoted in Step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the ברייתא of אבטולמוס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The אושא ruling mentions שביעית as if it were responding to an earlier view, but no earlier view on שביעית was stated.

steps.title: The ברייתא is missing a line
steps.stepSummary: A clause is missing from the ברייתא. The five elders actually said that an אתרוג follows its picking for מעשר and its budding for שביעית. אושא then said it follows its picking for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Something is missing, and this is what it teaches: an אתרוג follows its picking for מעשר, and its budding for שביעית. And our Rabbis voted in אושא and said: an אתרוג follows its picking, both for מעשר and for שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fills in the missing words of the ברייתא so that it reads smoothly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the missing clause is added, the disagreement becomes clear. The elders said שביעית follows חנטה, and אושא changed this so that שביעית follows לקיטה. This also confirms why our משנה, which follows אושא, treats a picked seventh-year אתרוג as שביעית produce.

keyTerms.meaning: It is missing words (the text is incomplete)
And this is what it teaches
The budding or early forming of the fruit
After, following

steps.whatToRemember: Five elders: an אתרוג follows לקיטה for מעשר and חנטה for שביעית. אושא: it follows לקיטה for both. Our משנה follows אושא.

phrases.english: It is incomplete, and this is what it teaches:
An etrog follows its picking for tithes,
and follows its budding for the Sabbatical Year.
phrases.notes: This is the part of the sentence that was left out.

phrases.english: And our Rabbis voted in Usha and said:
An etrog follows its picking,
both for tithes and for the Sabbatical Year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of Step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא mentions שביעית with no earlier statement about it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The elders had said that שביעית follows חנטה. אושא disagreed and ruled that it follows לקיטה.

steps.title: Inference from the משנה: a seventh-year לולב is holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the לולב in our משנה. A לולב may be bought only because it grew in the sixth year, which implies that a seventh-year לולב is holy with קדושת שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason a לולב may be bought is that it is a sixth-year לולב entering the seventh year. This implies that a seventh-year לולב is holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from our משנה. This is a setup line that prepares the challenge coming in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה allows buying the לולב only because it is from the sixth year. It follows that a לולב from the seventh year would have שביעית holiness, so it could not be bought in the usual way.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason
Belonging to the sixth year
This implies (introduces an inference)
Holy, here meaning it has קדושת שביעית

phrases.english: The reason is that the lulav is of the sixth year
that is entering the seventh year;
this implies that one of the seventh year is holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּלוּלָב בַּר שִׁשִּׁית הַנִּכְנָס לִשְׁבִיעִית הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the אתרוג back to the לולב in our משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Based on our משנה, a לולב that grew in the seventh year has קדושת שביעית.

steps.title: Why should a לולב be holy? It is only wood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the inference. A לולב is just wood, and wood has no קדושת שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? It is merely wood, and wood has no קדושת שביעית!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the inference from Step 5. It asks how a לולב could be holy when it is only wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קדושת שביעית applies to produce used for things like eating. A לולב is not food. It is a wooden branch, so it should not have שביעית holiness at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
Merely wood
The holiness of seventh-year produce

phrases.english: Why? It is merely wood,

phrases.aramaic: וְעֵצִים אֵין בָּהֶן מִשּׁוּם קְדוּשַּׁת שְׁבִיעִית!
phrases.english: and wood is not subject to the sanctity of the Sabbatical Year!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference made in Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that a seventh-year לולב is holy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wood has no קדושת שביעית, and a לולב is wood, so it should not be holy.

steps.title: Proof that wood has no קדושת שביעית: reed and vine leaves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a source about reed leaves and vine leaves. If they were gathered for eating, they have קדושת שביעית. If they were gathered for wood, they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: reed leaves and vine leaves that one piled up for storage on the field — if he gathered them for eating, they have קדושת שביעית. If he gathered them for wood, they do not have קדושת שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its challenge with a source showing that wood has no שביעית holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same leaves can be holy or not, depending on what they are meant for. Leaves meant for food are holy, and leaves meant for fuel are not. This proves that wood has no קדושת שביעית, which makes the challenge about the לולב stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: Reed leaves
Vine leaves
Piled them up for storage

steps.confusionAlert: The leaves are not holy or unholy by their nature. What decides it is the purpose they were gathered for: food or fuel.

phrases.english: (As we learned:) reed leaves and vine leaves
that one piled up for storage on the field,
if he gathered them for eating —
they are subject to the sanctity of the Sabbatical Year;
if he gathered them for wood (fuel) —
they are not subject to the sanctity of the Sabbatical Year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to back up the challenge in Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that wood has no קדושת שביעית
steps.raayaSupportSource: The source about reed leaves and vine leaves gathered for food or for wood

steps.title: The leaves source only excludes fuel wood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the source about leaves is a special case. The Torah only excludes things whose benefit comes after they are used up, like fuel wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the verse says: 'For you, for food.' 'For you' is like 'for food': it covers only something whose benefit and whose using-up happen at the same time. This excludes wood, whose benefit comes after it is used up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from steps 6-7. The leaves gathered 'for wood' have no קדושת שביעית only because they are fuel, and the Torah excludes fuel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says שביעית produce is 'לכם לאכלה', meaning for you, for food. Food is used up at the very moment you enjoy it. So קדושת שביעית applies only to things used that way. Fuel wood burns first and gives its real benefit afterward, from the coals and heat, so it is excluded. A לולב is not fuel, so it can still have קדושת שביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; that case has a special reason
'For you, for food': the פסוק (ויקרא כה:ו) about eating שביעית produce
Similar to; compared to
Benefit, enjoyment
Here: the using up or destroying of the item

steps.confusionAlert: Here בִּיעוּר does NOT mean the famous מצוה of removing שביעית produce from the house. In this sugya it simply means the moment the item is used up or destroyed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key test for the rest of the sugya. קדושת שביעית applies when the benefit and the using-up happen together.

phrases.english: It is different there,
because the verse says: 'For you, for food.'
'For you' is similar to 'for food':
phrases.notes: The two words next to each other in the פסוק teach about each other.

phrases.english: something whose benefit and whose using-up happen at the same time.
This excludes wood,
whose benefit comes after it is used up.
phrases.notes: Fuel wood burns away first. The real use comes afterward, from the coals that heat the oven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Deflects the proof from the leaves source. That source is limited to fuel wood.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a specific category (fuel whose benefit comes after use)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All wood, including a לולב, has no קדושת שביעית.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only wood whose benefit comes after its use, like fuel, is excluded by 'לכם לאכלה'. A לולב can have קדושת שביעית.

steps.title: What about wood burned for warmth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that some wood gives its benefit right as it burns, such as wood burned for warmth. Why should all wood be excluded?
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is wood used for heating, whose benefit and using-up happen at the same time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule from step 8. Not all wood gives its benefit only later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said wood is excluded because its benefit comes after it is used up. But when someone burns wood to warm himself, he feels the heat while it burns. That wood seems to match food exactly, so why exclude it?

keyTerms.meaning: But there is (a challenging counter-example)
Wood used for warming (רבינו חננאל)

phrases.english: But there is wood used for heating,
whose benefit and using-up happen at the same time!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the blanket exclusion of wood made in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that wood's benefit always comes after its use
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A counter-example: wood burned for warmth gives benefit while burning, just like food.

steps.title: Ordinary wood is assumed to be fuel
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that we judge wood by its normal use. Ordinary wood is meant for fuel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Ordinary wood is set aside for fuel.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge from step 9. We follow the normal use of wood, and normally wood is burned as fuel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wood can be burned for warmth, but that is not its usual purpose. The law follows what wood is usually used for, which is fuel, such as heating an oven with coals. Fuel's benefit comes after it is used up, so plain wood stays excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary, unspecified, not designated for a special use
Fuel, kindling for heating an oven

phrases.english: רבא said:
Ordinary wood is set aside for fuel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the counter-example of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case by its typical use
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since some wood gives benefit right away, wood should not be excluded as a category.
steps.terutzMaskana: We follow the normal use of wood, which is fuel, so ordinary wood is excluded.

steps.title: Fuel wood is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that the status of things whose benefit comes after use is debated by תנאים. It quotes a ברייתא about soaking flax and laundering.
steps.simpleTranslation: And whether fuel wood is excluded is a dispute between תנאים, as a ברייתא teaches: One may not hand over שביעית produce for soaking flax or for laundering. רבי יוסי says: One may hand it over.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a new point. The rule from step 8 is not accepted by everyone, and it shows this with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Soaking flax in wine, or washing clothes with it, uses up the wine. The real benefit, wearing the garment, comes later, just like fuel wood. The תנא קמא forbids it, which matches step 8. רבי יוסי allows it, so for him things whose benefit comes later still have קדושת שביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
One hands over or transfers (produce for a use)
Soaking (flax, to prepare it for spinning)
Laundering

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this ברייתא is about wood. It is about using שביעית produce, like wine, for soaking or laundering. It has the same structure as fuel wood: the item is used up first, and the benefit comes later.

phrases.english: And fuel wood is a dispute between תנאים,
as it is taught in a ברייתא:
One may not hand over seventh-year produce
not for soaking flax and not for laundering.
רבי יוסי says: One may hand it over.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the rule, the גמרא notes that the rule itself is a מחלוקת תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether things whose benefit comes after their use have קדושת שביעית is debated. The תנא קמא forbids; רבי יוסי permits.

steps.title: The reason of the תנא קמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the תנא קמא learns from 'for food': שביעית produce is for eating, not for soaking or laundering.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the first תנא? Because the verse says 'for food', and not for soaking and not for laundering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the תנא קמא's ruling and gives it right away: the word 'לאכלה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says שביעית produce is 'for food'. The תנא קמא reads this as a limit on how the produce may be used. Soaking and laundering are not like eating, so they are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: What is his reason?
The first (unnamed) תנא in the ברייתא

phrases.english: What is the reason of the first תנא?
Because the verse says: 'For food,'
and not for soaking and not for laundering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first side of the ברייתא quoted in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source of the תנא קמא's ruling
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לאכלה': the produce is for eating-type uses, not soaking or laundering.

steps.title: The reason of רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יוסי learns from 'for you': the produce may be used for all your needs, even soaking and laundering.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יוסי? The verse says 'for you', meaning for all your needs, even soaking and laundering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the source for רבי יוסי's opposite ruling, from the word 'לכם'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי focuses on the word 'for you' in the same פסוק. He reads it broadly: the produce may serve any of your needs. So even uses whose benefit comes later are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: For all your needs
And even

phrases.english: What is the reason of רבי יוסי?
The verse says: 'For you,'
'for you' means for all your needs,
and even for soaking and for laundering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 12; explains the other side of the dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source of רבי יוסי's ruling
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לכם': for all your needs, including soaking and laundering.

steps.title: How does the תנא קמא explain 'for you'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the תנא קמא deals with the word 'for you', which seems to support רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the first תנא, isn't 'for you' written?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the תנא קמא. The word 'לכם' is in the פסוק, so what does he do with it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי built his view on 'for you'. The תנא קמא cannot ignore a word in the פסוק. The גמרא wants to know what he learns from it.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written!

phrases.english: And the first תנא: isn't 'for you' written?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי יוסי's source (step 13) to question the תנא קמא (step 12).
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא קמא's reading of the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'לכם' seems to permit all uses. How can the תנא קמא limit the produce to food-like uses?

steps.title: 'For you' is read together with 'for food'
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא reads 'for you' as linked to 'for food'. Only uses where benefit and using-up come together are allowed, which excludes soaking and laundering.
steps.simpleTranslation: That 'for you' is like 'for food': something whose benefit and using-up happen together. This excludes soaking and laundering, whose benefit comes after they are used up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תנא קמא does use 'לכם', but he reads it together with 'לאכלה'. This is the same reading we saw in step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, 'for you' does not mean every need. It means needs like eating, where the benefit happens while the item is used up. Soaking and laundering use up the produce first and give benefit later, so they are excluded. This shows that step 8's rule follows the תנא קמא, while רבי יוסי disagrees.

keyTerms.meaning: That one (that same word)
Are excluded

steps.whatToRemember: The rule 'לכם דומיא דלאכלה' gives קדושת שביעית only to things whose benefit and using-up happen together. That is why fuel wood is excluded but a לולב is not. This rule follows the תנא קמא. רבי יוסי holds that 'לכם' includes all your needs.

phrases.english: That 'for you' is similar to 'for food':
something whose benefit and using-up happen at the same time,
which excludes soaking and laundering,
whose benefit comes after the item is used up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by repeating the reading from step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the verse: the word is linked to its neighbor
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'לכם' means all your needs, which would support רבי יוסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לכם' is limited by 'לאכלה' to uses where benefit and using-up happen together.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The fuel-wood exclusion follows the תנא קמא, who reads 'לכם' as like 'לאכלה'. רבי יוסי disagrees.

steps.title: What does רבי יוסי do with the word 'for food'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי: the פסוק says 'לאכלה', which seems to limit שביעית produce to eating only.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יוסי, isn't it written 'for food'?
steps.whatsHappening: Earlier, the גמרא asked how the תנא קמא handles 'לכם'. Now it asks the reverse question: how does רבי יוסי handle 'לאכלה'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא used 'לאכלה' to forbid soaking and laundering. רבי יוסי allows them, so the word 'לאכלה' seems to go against him. The גמרא wants to know what that word teaches according to his view.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written: a formula for raising a פסוק that seems to contradict someone's view
'For food': the word in the פסוק about שביעית produce

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei,
isn't it written: "for food"!
phrases.notes: This word seems to limit the produce to eating only.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 14. That step challenged the תנא קמא with 'לכם'. This one challenges רבי יוסי with 'לאכלה'.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי, who permits soaking and laundering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'לאכלה' seems to restrict the produce to eating, which would rule out laundering.

steps.title: 'For food' comes to exclude a medical poultice
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי needs 'לאכלה' to teach something else: the produce is for food, and not for a מלוגמא (a medical poultice).
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs that word to teach: 'for food', and not for a poultice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי does not ignore 'לאכלה'. He uses it to forbid a different use: turning the produce into a poultice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides now agree that 'לאכלה' excludes something. They only disagree about what it excludes. The תנא קמא says it excludes laundering. רבי יוסי says it excludes a מלוגמא, which is a crushed-food compress placed on a wound.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs that verse for something else: the word teaches a different law
A poultice or compress made from crushed food and put on the body as a remedy

phrases.english: He needs that [word] for
"for food", and not for a poultice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the word: 'לאכלה' is used for a different exclusion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'לאכלה' rules out laundering, which would contradict רבי יוסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יוסי, 'לאכלה' rules out only a מלוגמא. Laundering stays permitted.

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches 'for food and not for a poultice'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the answer with a ברייתא that says the same thing: 'לאכלה' excludes a poultice.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: 'for food', and not for a poultice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that this reading is not invented. A ברייתא already teaches it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Quoting the ברייתא proves that 'לאכלה' excluding a מלוגמא is an established teaching. The next lines of the ברייתא explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: As it is taught: "for food", and not for a poultice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the תירוץ of step 17 with a source.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that 'לאכלה' excludes a מלוגמא
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that states 'לאכלה ולא למלוגמא'

steps.title: Maybe 'for food' excludes laundering instead?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks itself: why say 'לאכלה' excludes a poultice? Maybe it excludes laundering?
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say 'for food' and not for a poultice? Or perhaps it means 'for food' and not for laundering?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, a question is raised. Why pick the poultice as the excluded use, and not laundering?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is exactly the תנא קמא's reading, which says 'לאכלה' excludes laundering. The ברייתא tests whether that reading could be correct.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you say this, or perhaps it means that? A ברייתא formula weighing two readings
Laundering

steps.confusionAlert: This question is still part of the ברייתא. The גמרא is not asking it in its own voice. The ברייתא is reasoning with itself.

phrases.english: Do you say: "for food", and not for a poultice,
or perhaps it is only: and not for laundering?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר ״לְאׇכְלָה״ וְלֹא לִמְלוּגְמָא, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא questions its own reading from step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which use does 'לאכלה' exclude: a poultice or laundering?

steps.title: 'For you' already allows laundering, so 'for food' excludes the poultice
steps.stepSummary: The word 'לכם' already permits laundering. So 'לאכלה' must be excluding something else: the poultice.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the פסוק says 'for you', laundering is already stated as allowed. So how do I explain 'for food'? It means 'for food' and not for a poultice.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. Laundering cannot be what 'לאכלה' excludes, because 'לכם' already includes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לכם' means 'for all your personal needs', and washing clothes is one of those needs. Since laundering is already allowed, 'לאכלה' must forbid a different use, and that use is the מלוגמא. This matches רבי יוסי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For you': for all your personal needs
So how do I fulfill (explain) this word? A formula for giving a word its purpose

phrases.english: When it says "for you",
laundering is already stated [as permitted].
So how do I uphold "for food"?
"For food", and not for a poultice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's question from step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לכם' already includes laundering, so 'לאכלה' must exclude the מלוגמא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the two words split the work for רבי יוסי. 'לכם' includes laundering, and 'לאכלה' excludes a poultice.

steps.title: Why include laundering but exclude the poultice?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא challenges itself: what reason is there to include laundering and exclude the poultice, rather than the other way around?
steps.simpleTranslation: What did you see that made you include laundering and exclude the poultice?
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. The ברייתא asks for the reason behind its choice, and the answer comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both laundering and a poultice are uses other than eating. So why should 'לכם' cover laundering while 'לאכלה' removes the poultice? The swap could seem just as reasonable, so the ברייתא must justify its choice.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? A formula asking for the reason behind a choice between two options
To include... and to exclude

phrases.english: What did you see to include laundering
and to exclude the poultice?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה רָאִיתָ לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַכְּבוּסָה וּלְהוֹצִיא אֶת הַמְּלוּגְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the division of the words set up in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's choice to include laundering and exclude the poultice
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both are non-eating uses. Nothing has yet been shown that makes laundering the better one to include.
